title: Semantic token scaling, dark mode mapping, and live-announcement grooming
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a focused review and grooming pass for: semantic token scaling (density + tone), dark-mode token mapping strategies, and live-announcement/focus-path behavior for the console component library. It synthesizes recent accessibility checks (axe/Lighthouse), design-team sketches, and a first-pass backlog of dev tickets. Goal is a lightweight, actionable plan to reduce regression risk during the upcoming theme migration.

Context
- We are migrating to a semantic token system where components read logical roles (surface, text-primary, interactive, border-muted) instead of raw hex tokens. This enables auto-adjustments across density and theme modes.
- Recent QA surfaced multiple regressions after a prototype dark-mode switch: insufficient contrast for subtle separators, missing focus outlines on compact cards, and noisy or missing screenreader announcements on modal transitions.
- This doc is a hybrid: design wireframe notes + a11y evaluation summary + grooming for engineering tasks.

Success criteria
- All primary text meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) in both light/dark at standard body sizes.
- Focusable interactive elements have persistent visible focus in high-density layouts.
- Live-region announcements for modal open/close and toast lifecycle are reliable across macOS VoiceOver + NVDA.
- Token mapping approach minimizes one-off overrides (target: <10% components needing per-component overrides).

Findings (high level)
1) Contrast delta gaps in dark mode:
   - surface-elev-1 (current mapping) reduces separation with page background; separators and subtle dividers fall below 3:1 against surface.
   - text-disabled and placeholder tokens drift too close to background at smaller sizes (12–13px).
   - Action: introduce tone-shift steps for critical tokens (text-muted-step1, step2) and enforce min-contrast checks in CI.

2) Focus visibility under density compression:
   - Compact card states (density scale -1) use 2px inner padding and a thin 1px focus ring; on many GPUs/monitors it becomes visually invisible.
   - Action: adopt dual focus strategy: a 2px focus ring + subtle box-shadow for compact layouts. Use prefers-reduced-motion media query for shadow toggling.

3) Live-announcements and modal focus handoff:
   - Modal opening currently sets focus to first tabbable; some modals perform async content updates and the screen reader reads nothing.
   - To ensure screenreader feedback, we need a short-lived polite live region with explicit message: \"Dialog opened: <title>\" and then focus the dialog container.
   - Action: implement aria-live polite message on open and ensure role=dialog with aria-modal and accessible name via aria-labelledby.

4) Token scaling across densities (voice of design):
   - Designers want semantic tokens to scale tone automatically: e.g., interactive-accent in dense mode should gain +6% luminance to preserve perceived vibrancy.
   - We need a deterministic mapping function (not hand-tuned) so changes are reproducible.
   - Action: propose a token scaler util (tokenScaler(theme, density, role)) that uses HSL deltas and clamps to WCAG thresholds.

Wireframe writeups (sketch descriptions)
- Compact table row state: show 3 density levels in a single frame. Notes: when density -1, increase row hover contrast by 10% and make focus ring 2px with 3px spread shadow. Include annotation calling out keyboard tab order and target area for focus.
- Modal stack example: wireframe shows nested dialogs and a toast on top. Notes: top-most modal gets aria-hidden applied to underlying content, and toasts announce with 'assertive' only for failures; success/info use 'polite' with brief message.
- Side rail nav: collapsed and expanded state. When collapsed, provide visible focus bar (4px) on left edge instead of full outline to preserve layout.

Accessibility test summary (recent runs)
- axe-core scan on staging with dark theme: 12 violations (vs 3 in light). Major categories: contrast (7), focus-order (2), region landmarks (3).
- Manual spot-checks: VoiceOver on Safari: modal open not announced if fetch delays >250ms. NVDA: focus ring sometimes not drawn on high-contrast Windows theme.

Proposed implementation plan (backlog groom)
Priority 1 (blockers/ship-safety)
- UX-945: Add CI contrast checker step for token mapping; fail build if any primary text <4.5:1. (owner: Marco)
- UX-946: Modal focus/announce pattern implementation + test harness for VoiceOver/NVDA. Include timeout-handling for async content. (owner: Leah)

Priority 2 (stability and polish)
- UX-947: Token scaler util prototype and RFC (tokenScaler) with sample outputs for 3 themes and 3 densities. (owner: Aisha)
- UX-948: Dual-focus style utility: focusRingCompact + shadow fallback; add prefers-reduced-motion opt-out. (owner: Design System)

Priority 3 (nice-to-have)
- UX-949: Automated visual regression snapshots for left-edge focus bar on side nav in collapsed state.
- UX-950: Accessibility lint rule for missing role/aria labels on dialogs created via portal.

Acceptance criteria (per ticket)
- Contrast CI: include sample token palette outputs + threshold report.
- Modal pattern: integration test that simulates 400ms content delay and asserts aria-live content emitted, plus screenreader smoke run recorded.
- Token scaler: RFC doc with examples, unit tests verifying WCAG clamping for edge colors.

Open questions / discussion points
- How aggressive should tone shifts be for interactive-accent in dark mode? (Design prefers subtle +6 to +12% luminance). We need empirical testing with user panel.
- Should toasts use assertive for failure states only, or also for security alerts that may be informational? Propose: failures/assertive; non-blocking info/polite.

Next steps (meeting + owners)
- Sync Thursday 9:30am PT: demo tokenScaler prototype and live-announce harness. Owners: Aisha, Leah.
- Grooming session Friday: break Priority 2 into smaller PRs, attach initial acceptance tests. Owner: Marco.

Appendix: quick checklist for reviewers
- Verify body text contrast across modes and densities.
- Test focus visibility on at least one Windows+high-contrast and macOS+retina display.
- Run modal open with simulated network delay.
- Confirm aria-live messages appear and are read by VoiceOver/NVDA.

Notes to self
- Keep token names semantic and predictable (avoid ad-hoc names like \"soft-surface-2\"). Map every visual variant back to a small set of roles.
- Capture before/after screenshots in PRs for any token remap.
